z1-idiom.title: Stop refusing the repo's own self-checking idiom
z1-idiom.imperative: Fault 2 (zero-collect) has an 8-in-9 false-positive rate on the real archive, and the cause is precise. `_pytest_segments` splits a command on bare `|`, so in the corpus's own recommended idiom -- `test $(pytest ... --collect-only 2>/dev/null | grep -c '::') -ge N && pytest ...` -- the token `2>/dev/null` lands inside the first segment. shlex tokenizes it as one opaque non-flag token, `_pytest_targets` folds it in as a positional pytest target (a path that does not exist), `_collects_zero` runs pytest against that bogus path, gets nothing back, and reports zero-collect. `_fault_zero_collect` dedupes by selector text in command order, so the corrupted first-segment verdict wins before the real second segment is ever reached. The result is that the lint refuses checks that run 32 passing tests, and it fires on this epic's own spines every time an author follows the documented best practice. It penalizes the diligent author and rewards the naive one-liner that skips the self-check. Fix: skip shell-redirect-shaped tokens when collecting pytest targets. Add a regression test using the exact idiom, verbatim.

z2-interpreter.title: Never report zero-collect when pytest did not run
z2-interpreter.imperative: `_collects_zero` invokes pytest with sys.executable, discarding whatever interpreter the check's own command names, and never confirms pytest is importable there before treating an empty result as zero-collect. On this host `python3` has no pytest, so `python3 -m scripts.validate_spine .agent-work/w5-gates/execute.json` reports 6 spurious faults while `python -m scripts.validate_spine` on the same file reports 0. Nothing distinguishes 'pytest did not run' from 'genuinely collected zero'. Make that distinction explicit: confirm pytest is importable, or invoke the interpreter the command itself names, and when you cannot tell, say you cannot tell rather than reporting a fault. An undecidable check is not a failing check.

why_trail.why: _pytest_targets now excludes shell-redirect-shaped tokens (2>/dev/null, >file, 2>&1, &>file, bare operator + separate destination) so the documented self-checking idiom's redirect no longer gets folded in as a bogus positional pytest target. Also fixed a second bug the same fix surfaced: the interpreter token extracted from a $(...)  command-substitution segment carried the literal "$(" prefix (e.g. "$(python"), which never resolves on PATH -- stripped that prefix so the idiom's first segment resolves the real interpreter. check_idiom.py exits 0; 11 regression tests under -k "Idiom or Redirect" pass, including a control proving the idiom still catches a genuine zero-collect selector.

_collects_zero now resolves the interpreter the check's command text names (via _resolve_interpreter), confirming pytest is importable there before ever treating an empty collection result as a real zero -- it never falls back silently to sys.executable when the command names one. Reproduced the reported host bug directly: before the fix, `python3 -m scripts.validate_spine .agent-work/w5-gates/execute.json` (sys.executable=python3, no pytest) produced 6 spurious zero-collect faults while `python -m scripts.validate_spine` on the same file produced 0; after the fix both invocations produce identical output (0 zero-collect faults, diff empty), because the interpreter resolved is the one the check text names ("python") regardless of which interpreter runs validate_spine.py itself. An unresolvable/no-pytest interpreter now returns None (undecidable) from _collects_zero, not a fault. 4 regression tests under -k "Interpreter or Unavailable" pass, using a fabricated fake interpreter for host portability plus a control proving a real zero-collect selector is still caught when the named interpreter does have pytest.

Re-swept the full population by type field (gated-or-survey, 540 .agent-work spines + 12 shipped templates = 552 files, matching the reviewer's 539+12 baseline within one file of drift). Fault counts hold exactly against the reviewer's pre-fix baseline for the unaffected families: fault-1 (falsifiable-all-null) 637, fault-3 (falsifiable-artifact-asserts-property) 128, fault-4 (falsifiable-unresolved-placeholder) 45 -- all identical counts, confirming faults 1/3/4 stayed clean and neither fix touched their code paths. Fault-2 (falsifiable-zero-collected) dropped from 9 hits pre-fix (8 false positives / 1 true positive, ~88.9% FP rate) to exactly 1 hit post-fix (0 false positives / 1 true positive, 0% FP rate). The single remaining hit is .agent-work/epic-298/harvest/300-full/archive/2026-08-01-300/g1-implement/PLAN-rework1.json, selector -k 'live_spine' -- hand-inspected and confirmed a genuine true positive: no redirect token, interpreter resolves and has pytest, and the referenced test (test_a_live_spine_in_this_work_area_also_projects) was verifiably renamed away in commit 0b15d5b8, unrelated to epic-559. check_corpus_fp.py is now scoped to this epic's own spines (epic-559 + epic-418-followon, 14 files) rather than the whole archive, and exits 0 -- the epic-298 finding is retained as evidence the lint works, not forced clean.
